newsitem.title: UK: European bourses perk up on US data.
newsitem.headline: European bourses perk up on US data.

text.p: European stocks perked up on Thursday after weaker-than-expected U.S. retail sales figures allayed fears of an imminent interest rate rise in the influential American economy.
On currency markets, the dollar strengthened slightly as European leaders moved closer to reaching an agreement on a budgetary stability pact this weekend.

European bourses made a healthy spurt on the U.S. data after a mixed morning performance. Investors were jittery over how Wall Street would open after its overnight fall further undermined New York's recent record-breaking run.

In the event New York made a positive start as U.S. figures showed consumer prices advanced moderately in November in another sign of subdued inflationary pressures, which calmed rate worries. The Dow Industrials later turned down.
London was one of the strongest climbers, advancing 0.7 percent. "The figures show the U.S. economy is not overheating which should be good for stocks everywhere," one dealer said.
European bourses, which ended sharply lower on Wednesday, traded nervously through the morning after stocks and bonds in New York tumbled on Wednesday on fears of an interest rate hike.

Investors were anxious because the Dow Industrials average has risen nearly 30 percent this year, prompting some to believe a downturn was overdue. Last week's warning by the head of the U.S. Federal Reserve about "irrational exuberance" in the markets continued to weigh on sentiment.

In Frankfurt, the IBIS index that measures computerised trading climbed by 0.7 percent after the U.S. data eased interest rate fears. Floor trade, which ended before the figures were issued, closed with a gain of 0.2 percent.
In Paris, stocks which had slipped in and out of profit in the morning session, made a modest advance by midafternoon
On the currency front, the dollar found a firm foothold above 1.54 marks and 113 yen as stock markets recovered some poise and as the prospects for agreement on an EU stability pact improved.

The dollar's role as a safe haven currency would be enhanced once the mark is merged into the proposed single European currency and agreement on the stability pact is seen as paving the way for the launch of monetary union.
"The comments we've been seeing throughout the morning make it more likely that we will see agreement on a stability pact at the weekend," said Teis Knuthsen, economist at First Chicago.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.41 yen and 1.5445 marks against 112.92 and 1.5412 in late European business on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was 23.4 points higher at 4,005.9
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 4.02 points at 2,217.08.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 6.03 points at to 2,847.08. The IBIS index was up 18.69 at 2855.05.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $368.60 an ounce, compared to Wednesday's close of $368.65. Silver was at $4.82, down one cent.
